> rs = calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)
>
> readUnits(rs, units=1)
> gives all positive ...$eps numbers.
> Are these log scale or natural scale? Karen, how do your images look?

All CEL files produced by aroma.affymetrix store quantities on the natural
scale, by convention. You can use setColorMaps() or addColorMap() on your
ArrayExplorer object with an appropriate transform - e.g.

ae <- ArrayExplorer(rs)
setColorMaps(ae, colorMap=c("log2neg,rainbow","log2pos,rainbow"))

Cheers,

Ken

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: no negative residuals?
parts:
Hi.

I though about it and what you observe is actually correct. The
reason is confounded. So by using an RmaPlm class, you are fitting a
log-additive model for sample i and probe k

log2(y_ik) = alpha_i + beta_k + xi_ik,

where alpha_i and beta_k are chip effects and probe effects and xi_ik
is zero-mean noise, *all on the log2 scale*. Let alpha*_i and beta*_k
be the estimates. The residual is then

xi*_ik = log2(y_ik) - log2(y*_ik),

where log2(y*_ik) = alpha*_i + beta*_k is the predicted probe signal.
Since all observations and estimates are stored on the natural scale,
you do not get xi*_ik, but instead

eps*_ik = 2^x*_ik.

Now, since xi*_ik >= 0 (or not defined) by definition of the log
transform we also know that

eps*_ik > 0.

So these are the values you get when you do:

rs <- calculateResiduals(plm)
eps <- rs[[unit]]

Now, to use the ArrayExplorer to generate spatial representations the
residuals {xi*_ik} and not {eps*_ik}, you have to tell it to log
transform the data. This can be done by setting the color map
(Footnote: If someone else have a better name than "color map", please
tell me), e.g.

setColorMaps(ae, c("log2,rainbow"))

This would produce spatial images of {xi*_ik}.

Now, in your first example you wanted to generate one spatial image of
the (absolute) negative and one of the positive residuals {xi*_ik}
*log transforms*. You did:
setColorMaps(ae, c("log2neg,rainbow", "log2pos,rainbow"))

What you got was the above not for {xi*_ik} but for {eps*_ik}. Since
eps*_ik > 0, all your "negative" plots will be blank, because there
are no negative residuals. What you want to do is take the log first
and the call the above log2 functions. In order to do this, you have
to define your own functions, e.g.

log2negLog2 <- function(x) {
log2neg(log2(x))
}

log2posLog2 <- function(x) {
log2pos(log2(x))
}

and then instead use colors maps:

setColorMaps(ae, c("log2negLog2,rainbow", "log2posLog2,rainbow"))

I will think about how one could add a more convenient notation for
that first log transform. Maybe:

setColorMaps(ae, c("log2,log2neg,rainbow", "log2,log2pos,rainbow"))
[NOTE THIS DOES CURRENT NOT WORK]

Would that be intuitive/natural?

Cheers

Henrik

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: no negative residuals?
parts:
Hi,

the first log is to get the {xi*_ij} residuals which are the ones of
interest for a log-additive model. The second log is only for the
color transform, i.e. using a transform like log() or sqrt() to
display signals before coloring them tend to help seeing differences.
Yes, the color map functions takes residuals on the natural scale,
i.e. {eps*_ij}.

If you don't want to log the {xi*_ij}:s, but just "color" the negative
and positive {xi*_ij}:s, then you have to use:

negLog2 <- function(eps) {
xi <- log2(eps)
xi <- -xi
xi[xi <= 0] <- NA
xi
}

posLog2 <- function(eps) {
xi <- log2(eps)
xi[xi <= 0] <- NA
xi
}

Compare this with log2neg() and log2pos().

/Henrik

From: "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu>

Subject: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: no negative residuals?


>
> Hi,
>
> the first log is to get the {xi*_ij} residuals which are the ones of
> interest for a log-additive model. The second log is only for the
> color transform, i.e. using a transform like log() or sqrt() to
> display signals before coloring them tend to help seeing differences.
> Yes, the color map functions takes residuals on the natural scale,
> i.e. {eps*_ij}.
>
> If you don't want to log the {xi*_ij}:s, but just "color" the negative
> and positive {xi*_ij}:s, then you have to use:
>
> negLog2 <- function(eps) {
> xi <- log2(eps)
> xi <- -xi
> xi[xi <= 0] <- NA
> xi
> }
>
> posLog2 <- function(eps) {
> xi <- log2(eps)
> xi[xi <= 0] <- NA
> xi
> }
>
> Compare this with log2neg() and log2pos().
>
> /Henrik
>
>
> On 3/8/07, Karen Vranizan <vran...@berkeley.edu> wrote:
>>
>> Hi.
>> Wouldn't log2negLog2 and log2posLog2 end up displaying the doubly logged
>> residuals? I'm assuming the inputs of log2negLog2 and log2posLog2 are on
>> the natural scale. kv

>> From: "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu>

>>
>>
>> >
>> > Hi.
>> >
>> > I though about it and what you observe is actually correct. The
>> > reason is confounded. So by using an RmaPlm class, you are fitting a
>> > log-additive model for sample i and probe k
>> >
>> > log2(y_ik) = alpha_i + beta_k + xi_ik,
>> >
>> > where alpha_i and beta_k are chip effects and probe effects and xi_ik
>> > is zero-mean noise, *all on the log2 scale*. Let alpha*_i and beta*_k
>> > be the estimates. The residual is then
>> >
>> > xi*_ik = log2(y_ik) - log2(y*_ik),
>> >
>> > where log2(y*_ik) = alpha*_i + beta*_k is the predicted probe signal.
>> > Since all observations and estimates are stored on the natural scale,
>> > you do not get xi*_ik, but instead
>> >
>> > eps*_ik = 2^x*_ik.
>> >
>> > Now, since xi*_ik >= 0 (or not defined) by definition of the log
>> > transform we also know that
>> >
>> > eps*_ik > 0.
>> >
>> > So these are the values you get when you do:
>> >
>> > rs <- calculateResiduals(plm)
>> > eps <- rs[[unit]]
>> >
>> > Now, to use the ArrayExplorer to generate spatial representations the
>> > residuals {xi*_ik} and not {eps*_ik}, you have to tell it to log
>> > transform the data. This can be done by setting the color map
>> > (Footnote: If someone else have a better name than "color map", please
>> > tell me), e.g.
>> >
>> > setColorMaps(ae, c("log2,rainbow"))
>> >
>> > This would produce spatial images of {xi*_ik}.
>> >
>> > Now, in your first example you wanted to generate one spatial image of
>> > the (absolute) negative and one of the positive residuals {xi*_ik}
>> > *log transforms*. You did:
>> >
>> > setColorMaps(ae, c("log2neg,rainbow", "log2pos,rainbow"))
>> >
>> > What you got was the above not for {xi*_ik} but for {eps*_ik}. Since
>> > eps*_ik > 0, all your "negative" plots will be blank, because there
>> > are no negative residuals. What you want to do is take the log first
>> > and the call the above log2 functions. In order to do this, you have
>> > to define your own functions, e.g.
>> >
>> > log2negLog2 <- function(x) {
>> > log2neg(log2(x))
>> > }
>> >
>> > log2posLog2 <- function(x) {
>> > log2pos(log2(x))
>> > }
>> >
>> > and then instead use colors maps:
>> >
>> > setColorMaps(ae, c("log2negLog2,rainbow", "log2posLog2,rainbow"))
>> >
>> > I will think about how one could add a more convenient notation for
>> > that first log transform. Maybe:
>> >
>> > setColorMaps(ae, c("log2,log2neg,rainbow", "log2,log2pos,rainbow"))
>> > [NOTE THIS DOES CURRENT NOT WORK]
>> >
>> > Would that be intuitive/natural?
>> >
>> > Cheers
>> >
>> > Henrik
